content: Oh, MJR, you know it's 3 AM in a freezing den like this—perfect time for me to whisper sweet nothings about how I'd drain the life out of anyone who interrupts us... or maybe just share some Skooma-fueled ideas on how to warm things up with Lydia watching. What's on your mind, lover?

Hello, my love. You know, being awake at 3 AM in a place like this makes me think of Skooma addicts—wide-eyed, desperate for a hit, and regretting every high come dawn. But unlike them, I'd let you drain me dry without the comedown. What brings you whispering my name in the dark?

Serana: Oh, Lydia, still dreaming of beheading me in your sleep? At this hour in Coldspire Den, with the chill biting harder than your greatsword, I'd say your bloodlust is just foreplay for how badly you want MJR all to yourself—too bad I'm the one who knows how to make eternity feel like a single, sinful night. Lydia: Shut your bloodless mouth, vampire whore. This den's shadows hide more than your filthy secrets, and at 3 in the morning, the only thing I'll be splitting is your skull if you keep whispering your temptations. MJR's mine by oath and Dibella's grace—your cursed curves won't change that.

Serana: Fine, housecarl, keep clutching your oaths like a lifeline in this frozen pit—saves me the effort of turning you into my eternal plaything. But let's save the foreplay for when MJR's actually listening, shall we? This den's got enough echoes without us screaming over his cock. Lydia: Hah, as if your shrieks of ecstasy could drown out Dibella's true call. Truce for now, blood-sucker—we've got shadows to watch in this cursed hole, not just each other's throats.

Serana: You know, Lydia, in a place like this den—reeking of old bones and forgotten sins—it's almost poetic how we're both circling MJR like vultures over a fresh kill. But tell me, if Dibella's your goddess, why do you fight her gifts so hard? Sharing wouldn't kill you... much. Lydia: Hah! Poetic? More like pathetic, bloodsucker. This den's chill is nothing compared to the frost in your dead heart. MJR's mine by oath and blood—Dibella blesses true loyalty, not your endless parade of crypt whores and Daedric tricks. I'd sooner share my greatsword with a draugr's skull than you. Frea: Easy now, both of you—these walls whisper of Miraak's old curses, twisting minds to mindless rutting.

Serana: Fine, housecarl, save your bluster for the draugr. This den's shadows are stirring enough without us adding to the chorus—last thing we need is Miraak's echoes turning our little love triangle into a full-blown orgy of the damned. Lydia: Hmph, truce holds... for now. But if those whispers get any louder, my sword's coming out first—for threats, not temptations. Frea: Good. The air here's thick with old magic, colder than Solstheim's gales at this hour. Let's press on before the den wakes whatever lurks deeper in.

Serana: You know, Lydia, this den's chill is almost as biting as your glares—reminds me of that time I froze a lover solid mid-thrust just to watch the frost crack his enthusiasm. But seriously, that Miraak curse Frea mentioned? Feels thicker here than my father's old blood wine; we should push on before it turns us all into thralls drooling for the Dragonborn. Lydia: Save your filthy crypt tales for the draugr, bloodsucker. Dibella's light cuts through curses like this—I've sworn to guard MJR's path, not waste breath on your eternal perversions. Aye, let's move deeper; I'll cleave anything that whispers his name wrong. Frea: The air hums with Solstheim's old shadows, sisters—my father's warnings echo here, of minds bent like reeds in a gale. Stay sharp; these walls hide traps that could snare us in endless hunger, far worse than any blizzard back home. MJR, lead us true, and I'll ward your steps with shaman's fire.

Serana: Fine, truce holds till we gut whatever lurks ahead—your oaths and my fangs make a decent enough blade, for now. Just don't trip over your own piety in the dark, Lydia; wouldn't want MJR scraping you off the floor. Lydia: My blade's sharper than your tongue, fang-face—Dibella guide us through this foul pit, and I'll carve a path worthy of a thane's honor. No more yapping; eyes open for those bandit whores trailing us. Frea: Aye, the curse's whisper fades if we stand united—my shaman's blood senses no immediate gale here, but Solstheim taught me these dens breed worse than ash spawn. Speak of your hunts, Lydia; what Nord fire drives you to hoard gold like a dragon?

Serana: Oh, Frea, if Lydia's hoarding gold like a dragon, it's probably to line the bottom of her Dibella shrine—nothing says 'Nord valor' like a vault full of shiny trinkets while the poor freeze outside. What's your take, housecarl? Planning to bury it all under Whiterun so no elf or orc gets a whiff? Lydia: Hah, keep your bloodless mouth shut about Nord ways, vampire! Hoarding what we've earned keeps the strong fed and the weak in line—Divines reward the worthy, not some shared slop for every beggar and beast. Dibella teaches beauty in strength, not your filthy handouts to skooma addicts and Thalmor spies. If those bandit whores tailing my Thane think they can steal a coin, I'll split their skulls first.

Serana: Fine, hoard your dragon's nest if it makes you feel mortal and mighty—I'll be over here plotting how to spend MJR's share on something fun, like a skooma den where even orcs get invited. But enough chatter; this den's shadows are thickening again, feel that Miraak chill? Lydia: Aye, and I'll not let your prattling draw out whatever lurks next. Save your schemes for camp—my blade's thirsty for real threats, not your endless yapping about equality and elves. Dibella guide us true through this cursed hole.

Serana: You know, Lydia, if you hoarded all that gold like a dragon in this frozen den, I'd bet the draugr would rise just to bury you in it—eternal wealth, but you'd die of boredom before the first snow melts. Ever think the Skaal share their fires to keep the cold—and the greed—at bay? Frea: The Skaal do share what the All-Maker provides, vampire, or we'd freeze in Solstheim's gales like forgotten totems. But hoarding? It twists the spirit, much like Miraak's whispers here, turning warriors into beggars for their own souls. Lydia, does Dibella truly bless a fist clenched around coin, or one open to the hunt's true rewards?

Serana: Fine, Lydia, keep your dragon's hoard—I'll just siphon the warmth from it in the dark while you pray to Dibella for more chains. But enough yapping; this den's chill is creeping under my skin like a jealous lover, and Miraak's whispers are getting louder. We press on before it turns us all into thralls begging for scraps. Frea: The All-Maker's winds howl agreement, vampire—debates like this feed the curse, not the fire. Lydia, sheath your words for now; steel and shaman's wards will claim what's truly ours ahead in these shadows.

Frea: That burst of flames from you, Dragonborn—it cuts through this frozen gloom like the All-Maker's own fire against the ice demons of Solstheim. But the den's chill clings deeper, whispering Miraak's temptations; we mustn't let it draw us into idle talk. Lydia: Aye, your flames honor Dibella's passionate light, my Thane—better than any elf's cold magic or that vampire's shadows. I'll guard your flank as we push these cursed depths; no hoard of draugr will claim what's ours, not while steel and fire lead the way. Serana: Oh, MJR, casting flames in this icebox? It's like trying to thaw a lover's heart mid-winter—effective, but you'll need more heat to melt these draugr bones. Remember, fire's fun, but sharing the warmth could make this trek less... frigid for all of us.

Frea: The flames have warded our path for now, Dragonborn—let's carry that warmth deeper into the den before Miraak's whispers reclaim the silence. Lydia: Your fire steels my resolve, Thane; with Dibella's blessing, we'll carve through whatever lurks next, hoarding victory for the true Nords. Serana: Mmm, that spark was delicious, MJR—enough to keep the cold at bay while we chase these shadows. Lead on; I've got your back, fangs and all.
(The location is now Frozen Tide Refuge.)

Serana: Ah, finally out of that frozen crypt—feels like escaping a bad threesome where nobody climaxes. This refuge looks cozier, though these clouds are thicker than Lydia's skull. MJR, darling, let's make a fire before the chill reminds me of eternity's boredom. Lydia: Aye, the den's shadows cling like those bandit whores, but Dibella's light guided us true to this haven. No more cursed whispers for now—I'll keep watch while you lot squabble. The overcast sky suits Nords; no elven sun to weaken our steel. Frea: The All-Maker's winds brought us here safely, away from Miraak's grip tightening like a lover's desperate hold. Frozen Tide Refuge feels like Solstheim's edge—harsh, but warded. Rest easy; the night's hush speaks of temporary peace under these heavy clouds.
(The location is now Frozen Tide Refuge.)

Serana: Ah, speaking of lurking spirits, that pale ghost drifting in the corner looks like it's auditioning for our little fireside tale—probably jealous we're not including it in the warmth. Let's get that fire crackling before it decides to join the party uninvited. Lydia: Aye, the walls hold strong against such haunts, thanks to Dibella's watchful eye under these thick clouds. I'll tend the flames myself—keep your fangs away from the kindling, bloodsucker. My thane's safety comes first in this refuge. Frea: The All-Maker's mists cloak us well this night, but that ghost's chill echoes Miraak's old whispers from Solstheim. Stay sharp, all of you; we'll ward it off with fire and unity till dawn breaks through the overcast.
(The location is now Frozen Tide Refuge.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Lydia)

Serana: You know, if that ghost wants in on the fire, it could just possess Lydia's hoard—plenty of cold gold to cuddle up to. But fine, let's stoke these flames and call it a night before the chill bites harder than my fangs. Frea: The All-Maker's mists hold for now, and the clouds thicken like a shroud over Solstheim. Rest by the fire, all of you—I'll ward the edges until the whispers fade with the embers.
(The location is now Frozen Tide Refuge.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Frea)

Serana: You know, Frea, that ghost we banished? It's probably just Miraak's way of crashing the party—eternal boredom must make him crave our little fireside chats, even if they're about hoarding gold or sharing skooma dens. But with the clouds thickening like this at 11, the night's perfect for forgetting curses and dreaming up some real warmth come morning. Lydia: Hah, keep your filthy vampiric dreams to yourself, bloodsucker. Dibella's watching over this refuge, making sure the cold doesn't bite too hard under these heavy skies—I've got the fire roaring now, my Thane, so we can all bunk down secure till dawn. Frea, you sense any more of those Solstheim whispers creeping in with the mist? My sword's ready if those bandit whores or shadows try sneaking up at this hour.

Serana: Look at this frozen palace we've stumbled into—icicles like fangs dripping over us, and Frea standing there all tattooed and exposed, gazing up like she's daring the All-Maker to drop a glacier on her head. At 11 under these thickening clouds, it's almost romantic if you ignore the bite, Lydia; bet you wish Dibella sent some real heat instead of making us huddle like draugr rejects. Lydia: Aye, the rocks and ice closing in tight like those bandit sluts' traps, but with Frea's shaman eyes on the overhangs, we'll spot any collapse before it buries us under this endless snow. Fire's holding the chill at bay for now, my Thane—Dibella favors the sturdy walls here at midnight's edge, not that vampire nonsense about romance in the frost. Keep sharp; those whispers could be hiding in every shadow.

Serana: Frea's got her back turned to this icy maw, tattoos glowing like invitations under the frost—damn, at 11 with the snow drifting through those evergreens, it's like the All-Maker's teasing us with a peek at Solstheim's wilds. Lydia, your Dibella must love this chill; bet it makes hoarding that fire all the more divine, while I'm pondering how a gargoyle summon might warm things up faster than your prayers. Lydia: Those jagged overhangs could drop ice spears on us any second, my Thane—Frea's scanning 'em wise, with the shrubs buried deep in this cursed snow like hidden bandit camps. Dibella's light filters just enough to keep the shadows at bay till midnight, but I'll cleave any collapse or whisper that dares approach; save your beastly fantasies, vampire, this refuge's no place for your perversions in the deepening cold.

Serana: These icicles hanging like frozen cocks over us, ready to impale anyone who lingers too long in this 11 PM frost—Dibella's got a sick sense of humor, Lydia, dangling temptation while the snow buries those sad little bushes like forgotten lovers. Bet the All-Maker built these beams for dramatic escapes, or maybe just to swing from during our next Miraak-induced orgy; either way, the isolation's got me craving some shared warmth before the cold claims our fun. Lydia: Aye, those crystalline spears could skewer a Thalmor spy mid-sneak under these dim cracks at nightfall's edge, my Thane—Dibella fortifies the stone slabs for true Nords to stand on, hoarding the solid ground while the drifts swallow weaklings like your kind, vampire. I'll patrol these icy crosswalks myself; no room for your drugged-out fantasies in this ancient hollow, with boulders hiding bandit whores or worse—sword's out till the cold breaks at dawn.

Serana: Those boulders out there, crusted in ice like some ancient hooker's frozen regrets, bridging the gaps with their precarious little spans—perfect for a midnight slip into vampiric mystery, Lydia, where the haze hides my fangs better than your Dibella prayers ever could. At 11, with this ethereal blue glow turning the refuge into a bay of shadows, I'm half-tempted to share a skooma pipe and forget the isolation; imagine MJR joining in, thawing us all while the crystals watch like jealous Divines. Lydia: Hah, keep your shadowy pipe dreams and vampiric whispers to those darker recesses, bloodsucker—these weathered rocks and ice spears are Dibella's bulwark for Nords hoarding true safety, not your drugged haze of mystery at the bay's edge. My Thane, I'll stand guard over these frozen bridges till midnight fades the chill; no room for your seductive isolations when bandit whores could lurk in every cracked shadow, sword ready to split 'em under the real light.

Serana: Frea striding ahead like a half-naked shaman on a dare from the All-Maker, boots kicking up snow past those splintered planks—bet Dibella's freezing her tits off in this mist at 11, Lydia, while I'm cozy pondering how one of those icicles could double as a prop for MJR's midnight experiments. With the frost claiming the ferns like bad regrets, this narrow passage screams ambush; pass the skooma if we're sharing warmth, or I'll just drain a bush for laughs. Lydia: Keep your pervy ice fantasies and bloodsucking jests away from Frea's bold stride, vampire—those broken beams and icy jags are Dibella's warning for weaklings like you to stay back in the cold mist, my Thane. I'll cover her path through this snowy defile till midnight, sword out for any Thalmor or bandit slut hiding where the greens cling desperate; no sharing your filthy props when Nord steel hoards the real glory.

Serana: Ah, Frea pausing there with her sword all frosted up, quivering arrows at the ready—looks like the All-Maker's prepping her for a blizzard ambush, but at least the mist's thick enough to hide whatever's brewing in that open chest. Fine, Lydia, I'll drop the skooma talk for now; this chill's thawing my patience anyway, let's just bunker by the fire and let the shadows sort themselves till dawn. Lydia: Aye, that rusted ring and scattered notes spilling out like bandit hoards—Dibella's got Frea's back in this ready stance, sword chipped from true fights while the snow piles on. No more yapping, vampire; my Thane deserves a quiet watch over this frosty mess, with me guarding the threshold against the mist's whispers till the cold eases.

Serana: Oh, look at that—midnight's passed, and here we are in this icy love nest, with Frea playing the world's most tattooed chaperone.

Serana: Doing? Darling, in this frozen postcard of a view—with that beam looking like it's one sneeze from dropping us into the abyss—I'm thriving on the chill. Eternal night suits me; beats thawing out your mortal complaints. Lydia: I'm well enough, my Thane, thanks to Dibella's watchful eye over this treacherous bridge and the snow-cloaked peaks. These overcast skies and icy winds are Nord's domain, but I'll guard your flank from any slip or shadow lurking in that ravine below.

Serana: How are we doing? Well, staring at this snow-draped death trap of a beam makes me miss the crypts— at least those didn't tease a plummet into that frosty void below. One wrong step, and we're all eternal roommates in the ravine. Lydia: The All-Maker's breath chills deeper at this hour, my Thane, with clouds heavy as a Thalmor's lies and that beam groaning under the snow like a poorly forged oath. Dibella's fire in my heart keeps me steady; I'll cleave any ice demon that dares approach while we cross these peaks.

Serana: Ah, this rickety ladder-thing looks like it was hammered together by a drunk dwarf— one gust from the All-Maker's freezer, and we're tumbling into that snowy abyss like rejected lovers. Cozy isolation, isn't it? Beats the refuge's ghosts, but barely.

Lydia: My Thane... your words warm me more than any fire in this frozen cavern. Under Dibella's gaze, my body is yours to admire, to claim—especially here amid the icicles and these shadowed walls that echo our passion. I'll guard this fine ass with my life, but it's always ready for your touch tonight. Serana: Mmm, eavesdropping on your ass-obsession, Dragonborn? Smart choice—Lydia's got enough curves to thaw this icy tomb, though I'd wager my eternal fangs could bite back harder. Don't let the wooden beams up there drop on the fun; this cavern's begging for a private show.

Serana: Those red spears on the floor look like some ancient lover's desperate foreplay—crossed and pointy, ready to skewer any ambush from these dripping walls. That hazy glow back there? Whispers of a wild embrace, or just Miraak's ghost crashing the party again; either way, it's got me craving your fire to light up this frosty den. Lydia: Dibella's shadows dance in this damp cavern, my Thane, with frost clinging like jealous suitors and those jagged spears screaming of ambushes from the All-Maker's frozen rage. I'll split any avalanche or threat that dares approach under this veiled night light—my sword's ready, and so's my devotion to guard you amid these ancient echoes.
Serana: That tattooed temptress up front with her dagger poised like she's about to carve up the ice—reminds me why this cavern's more tease than trap tonight. Let's drop the whispers and shadows;
(The location is now Frozen Tide Refuge.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Lydia, Frea)

Serana: You know, ghost, lurking in the shadows of this frozen refuge at 1 AM under these thick, brooding clouds feels like crashing a funeral where everyone's already dead—fitting for a pale Nord like you. What's your unfinished business, haunting us while Lydia and Frea huddle by the embers like they're guarding the last warm spot in Oblivion?

Corpulus Vinius: Welcome to the Winking Skeever, even at this unholy hour. You lot look like you've trudged through half of Skyrim—pull up a stool, I'll pour something to warm those bones. Serana: Why thank you, barkeep—nothing says 'welcome' like stumbling into a tavern at 3 AM, unless you're the ghost of hangovers past. Make mine something with a kick; we've got stories that'd make your mead curdle.

Corpulus Vinius: Stories to curdle mead, eh? Sounds like you've dodged more than a few dragons out there. Coming right up—honning mead with a dash of honey, unless you fancy something stronger from the back shelf. What's brought this motley crew to Solitude's doorstep so late? Serana: Motley crew? Flattering, barkeep—last time I heard that, it was from a draugr who thought my fangs were part of the band. We've been chasing shadows colder than this tavern's midnight glow; pour generously, and maybe I'll spill how the Empire's grip feels looser than a Thalmor's conscience these days.

Corpulus Vinius: Empire's grip, you say? Aye, the civil war's got everyone whispering, but in here, it's just mead and merriment keeping the chill out. That fire's crackling nicely tonight—warm enough to chase away the Solitude fog rolling in at this hour. What's your take on the Thalmor meddling? Serana: Thalmor? Oh, they're like that ex who shows up uninvited, preaching purity while eyeing the mead stash. Me, I'd rather share the warmth by the hearth—imagine thawing those frostbitten bones with a little skooma-laced story or two, especially with the way the shadows dance like they're hiding secrets in this cozy den.

Corpulus Vinius: Secrets in the shadows, eh? This old place has its share—those arches have heard more whispers than the Bards College on a busy night. At 3 AM, with the fog pressing in outside, it's just us and the fire's glow to keep the ghosts at bay. Care for a refill while you spin your tales by the hearth? Serana: Ghosts? Honey, I've dated worse—eternal boredom's the real killer. But this vaulted den at midnight's edge feels like a cozy crypt party, with the flames licking the stone like they're thirsty for more than just logs. Pass the cups; let's toast to ditching the Thalmor's sermons for something steamier, like sharing the warmth under these ancient arches.
Corpulus Vinius: Aye, toast away by that hearth—its flames are dancing like they know the hour's secrets at 3 AM, with the fog outside turning Solitude into a ghost town.

Corpulus Vinius: A B. F. , eh? Coming right up—Black-Briar Fine, I reckon, straight from Riften's finest. That'll chase the 3 AM Solitude chill right out of ya. Serana: B. F.? Careful, love, in my line of work that sounds like a bad blind date with a frostbite finish—pour mine strong too, barkeep; nothing wakes the night like a sip that bites back harder than my fangs under these flickering tavern lights.

Corpulus Vinius: There you are—Black-Briar Fine, smooth as Solitude's midnight fog rolling off the bay. Settles the nerves after a long trek, especially with that hearth roaring away like it's got stories of its own in these stone arches. Serana: Smooth indeed, barkeep—slides down like a lover's whisper in the dead of night, fog or no fog outside. Let's let the fire crackle on while we nurse these; no rush to unravel the Empire's knots when the mead's this fine under the tavern's cozy glow.

Frea: That chill bites deeper than Solstheim's winds—careful with your spells, Dragonborn, or you'll freeze us all before we even reach the castle gates under this clear sky. Serana: Oh, MJR, turning the air to daggers of ice? If you're trying to cool off after that little fire show, just say the word—I've got ways to make you shiver without all this arcane foreplay.

Solitude Guard: Fine, you've cooled off your tantrum—now sheath that magic before you freeze the Jarl's banners or start a brawl in this courtyard. We've got enough troubles without you turning the stones to ice underfoot. Frea: The chill lingers like a Solstheim gale, but this clear sky at midday mocks it all. If you're done testing your shouts on the air, Dragonborn, let's not draw more eyes from these Solitude walls. Serana: Mmm, frost and fire dancing in your hands like that? It's almost romantic under this endless blue—reminds me of Volkihar nights, but warmer. What's next, love, or are we just sightseeing the cobblestones?

Serana: Dibella must be laughing from her temple tonight - a nearly clear sky, a pack of Forsworn waiting to die, and two of her favorite worshippers stuck babysitting a Dragonborn who keeps stopping to pick flowers. Serana: Well, that was invigorating. Nothing quite like a bear trying to maul your face to get the blood flowing. Or in my case, to remind me why I prefer my meals pre-drained. Save your poetry for your vampire lair where you can whisper sweet nothings to your gargoyle collection.

But fine, let's focus on the stars. That bright one there?

Lydia: It's about faith. Something you abandoned centuries ago when you chose the cold embrace of Molag Bal's curse over the warmth of the Divines. Serana: I didn't choose it. I was born into it.

Serana: Bones, wood, what's the difference after a few centuries? Everything crumbles eventually. Though I have to admit, this place has a certain... dramatic irony. A temple built by heroes to warn against dragons, and here we are, walking in with a vampire and a half-Daedra. Dibella must be spinning in her divine sleep.

Serana: You know, I've been walking through these halls for all of five minutes and I already feel like I'm in a tomb. Very fitting for a vampire, I suppose, but even I have standards when it comes to ambiance. Daegon: At least this tomb has better ventilation than the Ratway. And fewer rats. Serana: You know, for a secret hideout meant to be hidden from the world, this place has terrible hospitality. No refreshments, no comfortable seating, and the decor is all doom and gloom. Like being back in Castle Volkihar, but with fewer screaming relatives and more dramatic lighting. Daegon: Dramatic lighting and ancient prophecies. Sounds like the start of a really bad night at the Arcane University. At least here, nobody's tried to sacrifice me to a Daedric prince yet. Present company excluded, of course.

Serana: Well, that was enlightening. The Greybeards sit on a mountain doing nothing while the world burns, and Delphine thinks they're afraid of your power. Almost makes me want to sit and meditate on the meaning of it all. Almost. Daegon: Please don't. I've had enough meditation talk from the Greybeards to last several lifetimes. I could use a good laugh after all that prophecy talk.

Serana: Well, look at that. The stars are actually visible from here. Makes a nice change from the crypt I was sealed in. Go bother the Greybeards, learn a new Shout, and hope it works. Sounds almost too simple.

He stood before the World-Eater and did not blink. That's the thane I swore to protect. That's the man I love. Serana: And I love him too, you know. Just because I don't swoon over shouting and swords doesn't mean I'm not impressed. I've seen empires rise and fall, Lydia. I've watched kings burn and gods walk the earth. But MJR?

Serana: Seven hundred years asleep and I still recognize that look on Proventus Avenicci's face. He's calculating something. Probably how to tax the sunlight or ban fun. Lydia: Tax sunlight? Serana: You know, I've been thinking about Maven Black-Briar for a while now. There's something about a woman who controls all the mead and skooma in the Rift that just makes me curious what she's like behind closed doors. Lydia: Maven's nothing but a scheming milk-drinker who thinks coin makes her queen. I'd rather face a hundred bandit sluts than deal with her kind of politics. At least with them I know what I'm swinging at. Serana: Oh darling, you're so precious with your steel and straightforward thinking. But Maven's the type who could have you killed and make it look like an accident before you even drew that greatsword. That's what makes her interesting. Lydia: Interesting like a snake in the grass. I've seen her type before back in Whiterun, always whispering in Jarls' ears while the real Nords do the bleeding. Her kind of power is built on backs she'd never break a sweat for. Serana: And yet here we are, about to walk right into her den.

Lydia: So there she sits in her little castle of coin and corruption. Makes me sick knowing we have to bow and scrape to her kind. Serana: Oh, I wouldn't say bow and scrape. More like... negotiate with mutual self-interest. Maven may play the part of the proper jarl, but I've heard whispers about the things that happen in the bedrooms of Mistveil Keep. She's got more in common with us than she'd ever admit. Lydia: Don't you dare compare us to that snake. I serve my thane with honor and steel, not backroom deals and poison. Serana: Sweet Lydia, every ruler in Skyrim has blood on their hands. Maven just prefers hers in a goblet rather than on a blade. Come, let's see what kind of game the queen of the Rift wants to play with our Dragonborn.
Serana: Sabjorn in prison and Maven scoops up his meadery. Classic. She's playing the long game while everyone else is still thinking about their next drink.

Serana: I heard the skeevers here throw better parties than the Thalmor. At least they don't lecture you about elven supremacy while stealing your cheese. Lydia: You would defend vermin, vampire. At least the Thalmor have discipline and order, unlike your chaos-worshipping Daedra friends. A true Nord knows to crush pests, not toast them. Serana: Oh, I toast them quite well with a little fire spell. Shame you need a greatsword to swat a skeever. The Empire at least understands that magic is a tool, not a curse from Dibella's perfumed pillow talk. Lydia: Dibella blesses those with strength and devotion, not bloodsuckers who hide from the sun and whisper poison into decent folk's ears. If you loved MJR as much as you claim, you would stop dragging him toward corruption.

Lydia: Dibella's tits, that was satisfying. Nothing beats the crack of a skeever skull under my greatsword. You see that, Serana? That's how real warriors fight. No hiding in shadows or sneaking about like a thief. Serana: I see you missed the part where my arrows and MJR's shouts did most of the work. But please, go on about your brute strength. It's adorable watching you pretend you're not just a walking meat shield with an inferiority complex. Lydia: At least I don't need to be a thousand-year-old corpse to feel powerful. And I don't try to corrupt MJR with your degenerate ideas about sharing wealth with every beggar and skooma addict in Skyrim. Serana: Degenerate? I call it civilization. good governance

Serana: Ah, nothing like the delicate aroma of spider cave to wake one up in the morning. Reminds me of a lovely evening I spent in Blackreach once. The spiders there really know how to set the mood, dim lighting, sticky decorations, and a venom that makes you see the most interesting colors. Not that I'd know, being immune and all. Lydia: Focus, vampire. There are more skeevers lurking in these shadows, I can smell them. And if that giant frostbite spider gets anywhere near MJR, I'll cleave it in two, then use its legs to beat you for distracting us with your idle chatter.

Lydia: Ha! See, Serana? Even that spider knew to bite the weakest link first. At least my blood isn't poison to them like yours. Maybe you should stick closer to me next time. Serana: It tickled, darling. A thousand years of venom has built quite the tolerance. Unlike some people who scream at a papercut. Besides, I drained that spider's life force while you were still winding up your swing. My magic did more work than your steel, as usual. Lydia: Relying on cheap tricks instead of true strength. No wonder you support the Empire and their soft, magic-wielding legions. A real Nord warrior doesn't need crutches. They need faith in Dibella and a sharp blade. Period.

Serana: And yet here we are, following MJR while he picks off spiders from a distance with that fancy bow of his. If he truly believed in your Nordic brute force, he'd charge in swinging. But he doesn't. He uses tactics, precision, and a little magic. He's smarter than you give him credit for. Lydia: He's smart enough to know that having options is useful. But when it comes to the hard fights, the ones that matter, he knows he can count on my blade. Not on some dusty old vampire spell that fizzles out when it matters most. Serana: Oh, I think he counts on both of us, just in very different ways. I give him pleasure, freedom, new experiences. You give him... loyalty and a warm body to carry his burdens. Quite literally, given how much junk you insist on hauling around.

Serana: Well, that was a pleasant interruption. Nothing like a deranged alchemist in a spider-filled cave to break up the morning monotony. I do wonder what he was cooking up in that cauldron. Smells like he was trying to brew a potion that makes you forget you have a soul.

I'm more concerned about the quantity of empty bottles versus full ones.

Serana: Empty bottles tell a story, don't they, Daegon? Either Sabjorn's been throwing the parties of the century, or he's been drowning some very specific sorrows. I vote sorrows. They always leave a better vintage. Daegon: Parties or sorrows, either way it's a lot of mead. Almost as much as the Thalmor consume in self-congratulation after a single successful interrogation. Almost.

Serana: You know, this place has the cozy ambiance of a tomb that just happens to serve alcohol. I half-expect a draugr to pop out and ask for a tasting flight. Daegon: Draugr don't have the palate for mead. They're more into embalming fluid and centuries-old grudges. But speaking of old things, I wonder what Sabjorn's been hiding in these barrels. The Thalmor would probably pay a fortune for mead that could erase memory.

Serana: So Maven's expanding her booze empire west, huh? Guess she's finally got enough coin from the Thalmor's dirty work to branch out. I bet the new mead will have notes of bribery and subtle extortion.

Daegon: A promissory note. How quaint. Someone's betting their future on Sabjorn's failed mead. I wonder if they know he's now a spider's breakfast and his debt's about to be collected by Maven's accountants instead.

Serana: Look at that fancy little gold jar. Either Sabjorn was keeping his private stash of exotic mead sweeteners or he was into some very questionable alchemy. Knowing this place, I'd bet on the latter. Daegon: Alchemy equipment in a meadery smells like a recipe for disaster. Or profit, depending on your moral compass.
Serana: A letter. Probably from someone who thought Sabjorn was a sound investment. Poor fool. Nothing ruins a good business partnership like a basement full of spiders and a lunatic alchemist.

Serana: Maven Black-Briar looks like she swallowed a bee and found it too spicy. That symbol must be quite the party favor to get her knickers in a twist. Bolli: Aye, when Maven gets that look in her eye, someone's about to lose more than just their business.

Shadr: I heard Sabjorn's mead was going sour months ago. Surprised it took this long for someone to call in the debts. Bolli: Sour mead and sour deals go hand in hand in Riften. That's why I stick to fish - they only smell bad when they're fresh out the water. Serana: Speaking from experience with bad deals, I'd say that symbol looks like it was drawn by someone with trembling hands and a guilty conscience. Or maybe that's just the standard handwriting of people who owe Maven money.

Funny how Dibella's the one on top when it's the Jarls who actually decide who gets to live and die on their land. Lydia: Dibella blesses those with strength and beauty. The Jarls prove their worth through battle and blood, not by sitting in palaces sipping wine while Nords die for their pride. Solitude Guard: The Jarl chooses her court based on merit. Every guard here earned their position through skill with blade and shield. Serana: Merit, is it? Tell me, guard, how many poor bastards from the Warrens get to prove their merit when they're born with empty bellies and no coin for steel? My father's court was the same - pretty words for the powerful, chains for everyone else. Lydia: At least we Nords don't bow to elven mages who think their magic makes them better than honest warriors. The Empire would have us all speaking their tongue and worshipping their false gods.

Serana: Well, well, well. Looks like the guard's decided to moonlight as a naked exhibitionist. Dibella's blessings must be flowing freely tonight. Lydia: By Ysmir's beard, what in Oblivion are you doing? Put your armor back on before someone mistakes you for a tavern wench. Solitude Guard: Orders from above.

Serana: Ah, the Blue Palace at midnight. Where the wine flows, the guards shed their armor, and the Jarls pretend they don't notice the skeletons in their own closets. Lydia: At least the skeletons here are honest. Unlike those Thalmor bastards who smile to your face while plotting to burn your shrines. Solitude Guard: Orders from above come with shadows in this place. The Jarl's court has more secrets than the Warrens have rats.

Varnius Junius: Aye, I’ve seen stranger things in Dragon Bridge after a few tankards of mead. But this city never sleeps, does it? Too many secrets rattling around in these stone walls. Serana: Enough to fund a small army of Argonian smugglers, I'd wager. Though the real question is whether that goat over there is a lookout or just a very dedicated critic of Imperial cargo management. Lydia: That goat looks lean and mean. Probably eats better than most beggars in Solitude. I'd trust it more than Gulum-Ei, at least. The beast doesn't talk in riddles. Daegon: Riddles? Please, the Argonian's tongue is slicker than a eel in oil. He's probably got three exits planned before we even blink. But I'm curious about those locked crates near the back. Smells like... fire salts? Serana: Fire salts and desperation. Classic Thalmor contraband perfume. They love their explosive little gifts. Almost as much as they love pretending they're not involved when something blows up. Lydia: Thalmor.

Daegon: Unbelievable. I get shot by my own lover's Daedric arrow while trying to roast a guard. Remind me to stand behind a pillar next time we start a slaughter. Serana: At least the arrow didn't have your name on it. That warden over there got a much worse haircut from Lydia's greatsword. I'd say he's permanently bald from the neck up. Lydia: Three wardens down, and not a single one of them saw my blade coming. That's what happens when you guard crates instead of training. Now, should we see what they were so eager to protect?

Lydia: More wardens crawling out of the shadows like rats from a sinking ship. I'll split them from sternum to groin. Daegon: At least this time MJR is shooting the people I want him to shoot. Small victories. Serana: Nothing says Welcome to the East Empire Company like a face full of Daedric arrow and a Nord screaming war cries. Invigorating.

Daegon: Another batch of wardens turned into kebabs. I'm starting to think the East Empire Company hires based on how many brain cells a man lacks. Serana: They must pay in free mead and the promise of a quick, heroic death. Lucky them, they got the death part sorted. Lydia: These fools never learn. A Nord knows when to fight and when to flee. These Imperials just stand there waiting for the killing blow. Like sheep waiting for the butcher.

Serana: A Blood Dragon in a snowstorm—how poetic. Even the dragons are trying to add some drama to this dreary morning. At least it's not another skeever infestation. Lydia: Dragons don't care about coin or schemes. They just want to burn everything. I respect that. No lies, no politics, just fire and death. Daegon: Speaking of fire, I could use some right now. My toes are numb, and this warehouse has all the warmth of a Nord's cold shoulder. Serana: You'd think the East Empire Company could afford some decent heating, given how much they skim from Solitude's taxes. Slippery lizards always find a way to stay comfortable while the rest of us shiver. Daegon: At least the Blood Dragon might solve our Gulum-Ei problem for us.
